title: Label-free Imaging of Biomolecules in Murine Brain Sections Using the 3D OrbiSIMS
protocol: Calibrate Orbitrap MS using SurfaceLab 6.7 control software.
Set up gas cluster ion beam \(GCIB) to provide pulsed beam of Ar<sub>3000</sub><sup>+</sup> clusters with energy of 20 keV and time-averaged current above 20 pA.
Set He gas pressure in secondary ion transfer optics to the “High” setting for optimal transmission of small inorganic cluster ions to the Q Exactive™ HF.

Navigate to Ag sample and adjust working distance \(sample-to-extractor) and target potential scheme to optimize secondary ion transmission to the Q Exactive™ HF. For a standard instrument configuration, use 1.5 mm and 57 V, respectively.
Calibrate mass spectrometer based on positive and negative ion spectra obtained from the Ag film using argon GCIB.
Section tissue in cryo-microtome with 10 μm thickness at -22 °C.
Thaw mount section onto conductive side of ITO coated conductive microscope slide for OrbiSIMS analysis.
Set up GCIB to provide a 20 keV Ar<sub>3000</sub><sup>+</sup> beam with a current greater than 1 pA.
Measure and record the beam current.
Set up electron gun to flood sample surface with > 10 μA low energy (20 eV) electrons for charge compensation between GCIB ion pulses.
Set He pressure in secondary ion transfer optics to the “Low” setting for optimal transmission of organic secondary ions to the Q Exactive™ HF.
Adjust target potential pulsing scheme to optimize secondary ion transmission to the Q Exactive™ HF mass analyzer for spectrum acquisition conditions.
Use in-instrument video camera system to find region of interest on tissue section.
Optionally, obtain a secondary ion image using a Bi<sup>3+</sup> beam and ToF MS to identify regions of interest for imaging with GCIB and Q Exactive™ HF.
Start spectrum acquisition using SurfaceLab 6.7 with a set mass resolving power of 240,000.
Set up 20 keV Ar<sub>3000</sub><sup>+</sup> focused pulsed beam with a spot size smaller than 2 μm and current between 1 pA and 30 pA.
Set up electron gun to flood sample surface with > 10 μA low energy electrons for charge compensation between gas cluster ion pulses.
Set He pressure in secondary ion transfer optics to the “Low” setting for optimal transmission of organic secondary ions to Q Exactive™ HF.
Adjust target potential pulsing scheme to optimize secondary ion transmission to Q Exactive™ HF mass analyzer for imaging conditions, using a sawtooth raster pattern.
Use in-instrument video camera system to find region of interest on tissue section.
Start image acquisition using SurfaceLab 6.7 with a set mass resolving power of 240,000 and an image resolution corresponding to the GCIB spot size.
Use a saw tooth raster pattern for the GCIB.
Inspect mass spectra obtained in steps 3 and 4 in SurfaceLab 6.7 and identify mass peaks of interest.
Set up the instrument for spectrum or image acquisition following step 3 or step 4.

Start spectrum acquisition from region of interest using SurfaceLab 6.7, selecting the option for tandem mass spectrometry using the higher-energy collision-induced dissociation cell in the Q Exactive™ HF.
Adapt normalised collision energy to the analyte; useful values are typically between 15 and 70 eV.
Inspect mass spectra in SurfaceLab 6.7 and review potential putative secondary ion assignments for peaks of interest.
Select peaks for image generation, ensuring that peak integration windows encompass the full width of the mass spectral peaks.
Adjust secondary ion intensity-to-colour transformation functions for individual images to highlight relevant features of the data.
Make composite multi-colour images, e.g., RGB, based on individual secondary ion images or summed images.
